title.en: Job offer that asks for money first

pattern.en: An 'employer' or 'agent' offers a job abroad and asks for a processing, visa, training or insurance fee before you start. Real employers and licensed agencies never charge job seekers (ILO Convention 181, Art. 7).

advice.en: Do not pay. Check the company on its official website and the national company register; ask for a written contract and verify the visa route yourself.

provenance.quote: Private employment agencies shall not charge directly or indirectly, in whole or in part, any fees or costs to workers.

pattern.en: Agents promise a guaranteed visa, a 'work permit for sale' or admission without certificates, often via WhatsApp or Facebook.

advice.en: No one can guarantee a visa. Only embassies and official visa centres take applications; compare the fee with the official fee in Njia.

title.en: Scholarship that charges an application fee

pattern.en: A website lists a 'fully funded scholarship' and asks for a registration or courier fee, or asks for your bank login.

advice.en: Government and university scholarships are free to apply for. Apply only on the funder's own domain (e.g. daad.de, chevening.org, stipendiumhungaricum.hu).

pattern.en: A 'provider' offers to open a German blocked account for a small fee and asks you to transfer the EUR 11,904 to a private or mobile-money account.

advice.en: Use only providers accepted by the German Embassy; transfer only to the provider's own IBAN; check the list on make-it-in-germany.com.

title.en: Recruitment of health workers from Sierra Leone

pattern.en: Sierra Leone is on the WHO health workforce support and safeguards list 2023. Active international recruitment of doctors and nurses from listed countries should follow the WHO Global Code and government-to-government agreements.

advice.en: Njia shows health-sector pathways for information but does not match health workers to foreign employers.

provenance.quote: 55 countries on the 2023 list: 37 in the African region.
